subject: Renewal + mid-term GPU uplift: sizing options & discount flexibility
messages:
From: Emma Sayers <emma.sayers@sparrowanalytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@sparrowanalytics.com
Date: 2026-09-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal timing + potential mid-term GPU add

Hi Monica,

Our Dedicated contract is up for renewal Nov 15 and the analytics team is projecting a 35-50% increase in peak throughput over the next 9 months. We want to explore options to: add GPUs mid-term to our existing pool, preserve our current committed discount band, and understand throughput SLAs if we bump accelerator count.

Key asks:
- Can we get a mid-term uplift without restarting the 12-month term?
- What discount flexibility is available if we commit to a 20% uplift today?
- Any guarantees on p99 latency/throughput if we increase the pool?

We'd like a short call next week to review options and get a revised quote for our procurement team.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Sayers
Head of Platform
Sparrow Analytics
---
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Emma Sayers <emma.sayers@sparrowanalytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + potential mid-term GPU add

Hi Emma — great timing. Thanks for the heads up. Short answers up front: yes, we support mid-term uplifts without resetting the remaining term; we can offer tiered uplift pricing depending on commit length; and we can guarantee throughput bands with a SLO tied to committed pool size and a simple overage protection model.

I'll attach two paths for you:
- Option A: 20% uplift now with a 12-month addendum (preserves your current discount tier + 4% incremental uplift discount).
- Option B: 40% uplift with a 24-month extended commit (larger discount, blended price smoothing).

I ran a quick capacity check and your region (us-west) has the headroom to perform this change with zero downtime. If you want, Karthik and I can join a short call to walk the procurement team through the quote and SLO language.

Attaching a draft quote and throughput test summary.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
Attachments: Sparrow_Dedicated_Quote_v2.pdf; throughput-test-results.csv
From: Emma Sayers <emma.sayers@sparrowanalytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T08:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + potential mid-term GPU add

Monica — thanks, received the quote. A couple quick clarifying questions before the call:

1) The draft shows a 4% uplift discount for Option A. Is that off list price or off our current committed unit price? Procurement needs the math line-by-line.
2) For the throughput SLO you mentioned: can you confirm the exact p50/p95/p99 token-per-second targets for our pool at the proposed 20% and 40% sizes? We run a mix of long-context and short chat payloads.
3) Are there any penalties or minimum-notice windows to scale down if our usage drops?

Can we schedule a 30-min slot Friday? Our procurement lead, procurement@sparrowanalytics.com, will join.

—Emma
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Emma Sayers <emma.sayers@sparrowanalytics.com>, procurement@sparrowanalytics.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + potential mid-term GPU add

Emma/procurement team — looping in Karthik (pricing lead) and Marissa (Customer Success for renewals). See inline answers and a suggested structure for the Friday call:

1) Discount math: the 4% is off your existing committed unit price (not list). We'll include the baseline unit price, your current committed discount, and the uplift adjustment line items in the quote. I'll export a CSV with per-GPU unit economics for procurement.

2) Throughput SLOs (rough band; we'll finalize after a short load test):
- Current pool: p50 120 tokens/s, p95 90 tokens/s, p99 60 tokens/s (mixed payload).
- 20% uplift pool: p50 ~145 tokens/s, p95 ~110 tokens/s, p99 ~75 tokens/s.
- 40% uplift pool: p50 ~170 tokens/s, p95 ~130 tokens/s, p99 ~90 tokens/s.
We can formalize these numbers into the SLO doc and include a clause allowing a one-week verification window post-activation to validate production performance.

3) Scale-down: we offer a 30-day minimum notice for reductions during the committed term. For mid-term reductions inside the first 60 days after an uplift we apply a prorated true-down fee (designed to cover the reserved hardware allocation). We'll add the exact formula to the addendum.

Proposed Friday slot: 2026-10-08 10:00 PT. Does that work?

Thanks,
Monica
From: procurement@sparrowanalytics.com <procurement@sparrowanalytics.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T10:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + potential mid-term GPU add — follow up and counter

Thanks all for the call earlier. Procurement reviewed the price model and ran the uplift math against our forecast. Two ask items from finance before we can sign: 

1) Can Redwood extend the 4% incremental uplift discount to 6% if we commit to the 20% uplift now and prepay six months of the uplifted portion? This helps our cash planning.
2) The scale-down clause with a prorated true-down fee is acceptable, but finance asks that the maximum true-down exposure be capped at one month of baseline committed spend.

If you can accept those two points, we can proceed to a redline-ready addendum and get approvals internally next week.

Best,
Sparrow Procurement
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: procurement@sparrowanalytics.com, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + potential mid-term GPU add — follow up and counter

Hi Emma / Sparrow procurement — thanks for the clear asks and for the productive call. Monica looped me in to handle pricing flexibility. Proposed final position: 

- We can increase the uplift discount to 5.5% (rather than 6%) if Sparrow prepays 6 months of the uplifted portion at the time of addendum execution. This keeps our margins while recognizing prepaid cash benefits.
- For the true-down exposure cap, we can accept a cap equal to 1 month of baseline committed spend, provided the cap applies only if Sparrow gives 30-day notice and reductions don't exceed 50% of the uplifted capacity within the first 90 days.

If that reads acceptable, Monica will issue a redline-ready addendum and updated quote (reflecting the 5.5% uplift discount and the capped true-down formula). We can also add a one-week verification window post-activation for the throughput SLO.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this.

Karthik Iyer
Pricing Lead, North America
Redwood Inference
